## Research projects

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
S-LAB, Jeonbuk National University · Feb 2026 – present
:::

[Transferability and Configuration Sensitivity of Clinical Prediction Models across Imaging, Time-Series, and Tabular Data](project-transferability.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
*N. Y. Kim*, H. Choi, H. Kim, G. Kim, S. Hwang
:::

Asks when transfer learning actually helps a clinical model, and whether the gain
survives the choices made while training it — seeds, splits, prevalence,
thresholds, and noise. Three tasks stand in for three kinds of transfer: breast
imaging, continuous glucose time series, and tabular COVID-19 outcomes.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-transferability.qmd){.research-btn}
:::

:::

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
S-LAB, Jeonbuk National University · Aug 2026 – present
:::

[Chest CT-Based Prediction of Pulmonary Function and Evaluation of Model Explainability](project-airway-ct.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
*N. Y. Kim*
:::

Predicts airflow limitation from hundreds of heavily correlated quantitative CT
measures, then asks whether competing explanations agree on *why* — not just on
*what*.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-airway-ct.qmd){.research-btn}
:::

:::

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
Department of Statistics, Jeonbuk National University · Aug 2026 – present
:::

[A Bootstrap Algorithm for Comparing Diagnostic Test Accuracy in Meta-Analysis with Within-Study Correlation](project-dauc-bootstrap.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
S. Hwang, J. Kim, *N. Y. Kim*, H. Choi
:::

Inference on a difference in summary ROC areas usually treats two diagnostic
tests as independent, even when the same participants took both. The paper
proposes a correlation-aware bootstrap that carries the dependence through.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-dauc-bootstrap.qmd){.research-btn}
:::

:::

## Conference presentations

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
Korean Data and Information Science Society 2026
:::

[Assessing the Reliability of Clinical AI: Reproducibility of Transfer Learning across Three Medical Modalities](project-transferability.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
*N. Y. Kim*, H. Choi, H. Kim, G. Kim, S. Hwang · November 2026, Busan
:::

Isolates one factor per task — the kind of source pretraining, the amount of
target adaptation, and whether a large source-domain stage exists at all — and
asks whether the gain survives being carried to another institution, country or
cohort. The direction of the gain held across all three domains; its size did
not.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-transferability.qmd){.research-btn}
:::

:::

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
Korean Data and Information Science Society 2026
:::

[Explainable AI under Correlated Features: Do Models Agree on Why? An Application to Airflow Limitation Detection from Quantitative Chest CT](project-airway-ct.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
H. Kim, *N. Y. Kim*, Y. Lee, K. Chae, S. Hwang · November 2026, Busan
:::

Three models detect airflow limitation from quantitative chest CT at nearly the
same accuracy, then are asked what they used. Before the correlated measures were
reduced all three credited emphysema first; afterwards they stopped agreeing,
while AUROC barely moved. Similar accuracy did not guarantee similar
explanations.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-airway-ct.qmd){.research-btn}
:::

:::

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
IC-KDA + ASAD 2025 · Best Poster Award
:::

[Effectiveness of Digital Cognitive Training Interventions for Dementia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis](project-dementia-meta.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
J. Sung, *N. Y. Kim* · May 2025, Seoul
:::

A PROSPERO-registered meta-analysis of eleven randomized trials asking whether
remotely delivered cognitive training improves cognitive and depressive outcomes
in dementia. It improved both, on a small evidence base.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-dementia-meta.qmd){.research-btn}
[PROSPERO](https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=631806){.research-btn}
:::

:::

::: {.research-card}

::: {.research-label}
Korean Statistical Society Summer Conference 2025
:::

[Deep Learning-based Neural Granger Causality for Solar Radiation Time Series](project-granger.qmd){.research-title}

::: {.research-authors}
M. Lee, S. Lee, Y. Cho, *N. Y. Kim*, G. Kim, Y. Lee · June 2025, Gyeongju
:::

Asks which meteorological variables carry predictive information about solar
radiation, and whether neural Granger causality recovers relationships a linear
vector autoregression misses. It does, for the variables that behave least like
continuous measurements.

::: {.research-links}
[Project page](project-granger.qmd){.research-btn}
:::
